item.name: Trip Search (Gateway)
item.description:
TA-17 one-way search: `GET /api/v1/trips/search`.

Requires a verified traveller, so run **Authentication (Gateway) > Sign In**
first -- these requests inherit the bearer `{{accessToken}}` it stores. There is
no guest mode.

The station, travel-class and train-number variables are the fixed ids of the
catalog search fixture; load it with `npm run catalog:seed:search` after catalog
has migrated. `{{searchDepartureDate}}` is filled in automatically with the Cairo
date three days out (the day the fixture puts trips on) whenever it is left blank.

Every response uses the platform envelope: `success`, `data`, `error`. A refusal
names the field to change in `error.details[].field`; a 503 or 504 from a slow or
stopped catalog carries `error.retryAfterSeconds`.

### TA-18: round trip, filters, stops and recent searches

The later requests cover the second half of the story. `{{searchReturnDate}}` and `{{searchToday}}` are filled in automatically like the departure date; `{{outboundTripId}}` is stored by **Round Trip - Outbound Leg**, so run that before the return call or the stops request.

The filter requests use the Tanta -> Ramsis pair, which the fixture gives two train types and two fares -- the only pair where a train-type filter and a fare sort have anything to do.

Recent searches are per traveller: sign in as somebody else and the list is empty, which is the rule rather than a bug.

item.name: Stations (Gateway)
item.description:
TA-15's bilingual station picker plus the operator-only station management routes: `GET /api/v1/stations`, and `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `POST :id/deactivate` and `DELETE` under `/api/v1/stations`.

Needs a seeded catalog and identity's seeded operator. From a clean database:

```
docker compose up -d
docker compose run --rm seeder
```

Run the folder in order. It signs the operator in itself, reads a real city from an existing station rather than hardcoding a seed id, then creates a station and follows it through update, deactivate and DELETE.

Three things the order is designed to show:

- **Authorization** — the picker is the only anonymous route; the station snapshot returns 401 without the operator token.
- **Cache refresh** — the list carries a 24-hour TTL, so *Picker Shows The New Station* and *Picker Drops The Deactivated Station* only pass because the station change invalidated the cache instead of waiting it out.
- **Lifecycle safety** — *DELETE Aliases Deactivate* followed by *Station Survives DELETE* proves a referenced station is closed, not destroyed.

item.name: Operations (Gateway)
item.description:
TA-20 operator-only writes: `POST /api/v1/operations/timetables`, `POST /api/v1/operations/fares` and `GET /api/v1/operations/audit`.

Requires the catalog search fixture, whose network now includes train 916 with a first-class coach and no timetable, plus identity's seeded operator. From a clean database:

```
docker compose up -d
docker compose run --rm seeder
```

Run **Operator Sign In** first; it replaces `{{accessToken}}` with the operator's token and records the account id from the JWT. Every write needs an `Idempotency-Key`. The publish request stores its key, so **Publish Retried with Same Key** can replay it and return the same `timetableId` and version.

The route is Ramsis (Cairo) to Alexandria. Search resolves the fare against the current instant, so **Search Again** waits for the fare's `effectiveFrom` before asking; otherwise the old amount is the correct answer.
